title: Old north road paving
subject: Subject: the paving of an old road on a cold northern moor, about 2.5 m across. Worn, roughly squared grey paving blocks of a few sizes laid in loose rows, their edges chipped and rounded; thin tufts of dry golden grass and a little white frost in the gaps, a few small patches where the blocks are missing and earth shows. Cold blue-grey night colours with warm straw-coloured grass.
use: The ground of the four roads at the northern crossroads.

title: Frosted moor grass
subject: Subject: rough moor ground in late autumn, about 3 m across. Dark peaty earth almost hidden under clumps of dry golden-brown grass, the blade tips touched with white frost, a few tiny pale stones. The clumps are of even size and spread evenly. Night colours: muted straw and umber with cold blue-violet shadow.
use: The open ground of the north: the crossroads moor, and any frosty grassland in the game.

title: Thin snow over moor grass
subject: Subject: moor ground where the first snow has fallen thinly, about 3 m across. Uneven patches of pale blue-white snow lying over dark earth and flattened dry grass, with brown grass tufts poking through; the patches are of mixed small sizes, spread evenly, none large. Moonlit night colours.
use: Where the snow begins: the crossroads' north edge, and the edges between grass and deep snow anywhere in the north.

title: The crossroads' compass ring
subject: Subject: the paved ring where four old roads meet, seen from straight above, about 14 m across. Curved grey paving stones laid in four or five rings, worn and uneven, with dry grass and frost in some joints, round a carved eight-pointed compass star in darker stone at the centre. The four roads' stubs leave the ring north, south, east and west, cut off at the picture's edges. Cold moonlit colours.
use: Laid as one piece in the middle of the crossroads, where Halcyon's ambush happens.

title: Ruined road gatepost
subject: Subject: an old square gatepost of grey cut stone, seen flat from the front, about 2.5 m tall: stacked blocks with a flat capstone, chipped corners, frost in the joints, and a few blocks of a broken low wall at its foot on one side. Moonlit night colours.
use: The four gateposts on the north and south roads at the crossroads.

title: The crossroads well
subject: Subject: the crossroads well, seen flat from the side. A round well of grey fitted stones about 1 m high, with a weathered wooden frame and crossbar over it, a rope and wooden bucket, and a small iron lantern hanging from the post on the right with its glass glowing amber. A folded letter held down by a small stone on the rim. The whole well is in the picture.
use: The well south-west of the ring, where the letter is.

title: The fallen waymarker
subject: Subject: an old waymarker pillar of grey carved stone, about 3 m long, lying toppled on its side, seen flat from the side. Square in section with a squared cap, worn carved bands along it, and one diamond-shaped rune near the cap glowing warm amber. Its broken base and a few loose stone pieces lie beside it. The whole pillar is in the picture.
use: North-east of the ring at the crossroads.

title: Dark moor pine
subject: Subject: one dark spruce-like pine, about 8 m tall, seen from the side, whole, with its trunk foot at the bottom. Deep blue-green needles in drooping tiers, a narrow pointed top, only a few flecks of frost. Moonlit night colours.
use: The pines at the crossroads' corners.

title: Bare dead tree
subject: Subject: one leafless dead tree, about 5 m tall, seen from the side, whole, with its base at the bottom. A dark twisted trunk splitting into thin crooked branches and fine twigs, no leaves. Night colours, almost black against the grey.
use: Among the rocks at the crossroads' south-east corner.

title: Leafless moor bush
subject: Subject: one leafless bush, about 1.2 m tall, seen from the side, whole, with its base at the bottom. Many thin dark brown twigs fanning up from a short base, a few dry grass blades at its foot. Night colours.

title: Frosted grass tuft
subject: Subject: one tuft of dry moor grass, about 50 cm tall, seen from the side, whole, with its base at the bottom. Thin arching golden-brown blades, the tips white with frost. Night colours.
use: Scattered thickly over the crossroads moor, to break up the flat ground.
